stories.headline: Cyclone ‘Akvan’ crosses Odisha coast, no damage reported
stories.title: Cyclone ‘Akvan’ crosses Odisha coast, no damage reported
stories.summary: Ganjam district and its adjoining areas receive heavy rainfall, with Patrapur (209 mm) recording the highest; several districts of West Bengal are battered by rain and flight and train services affected
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Odisha government on Friday (November 20, 2026) said no human casualty and damage to infrastructure were reported when cyclone Akvan crossed the State’s coast near Gopalpur, causing heavy rain in south-coastal and coastal districts early in the morning.
Several districts of West Bengal were battered by rain and flight and train services were affected in the State due to the cyclone impact.
The cyclone had considerably lost its intensity when it made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha.

“The cyclonic storm Akvan crossed the south coastal Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh close to Gopalpur with a wind speed of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph during 7.30 a.m. to 8.30 a.m.,” said the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
“Except low-lying areas in urban regions filled with rainwater, everything is under control.
There were 12 blocks in Ganjam district those recorded more than 100 mm rainfall during 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m.,” said Anu Garg, Chief Secretary of Odisha.
Ganjam district and its adjoining areas received heavy rainfall with Patrapur (209 mm) recording highest rainfall.
After cyclone crossed the coast near Gopalpur, coastal areas such as Kendrapada, Baleshwar, Chandbali, Kataka and Paradip received more than 30 mm rainfall.
During the day, Kendrapada recorded highest 57 mm rainfall.
IMD sources said the cyclone first weakened into deep depression, subsequently to depression and finally well-marked low pressure area during the day.
In view of the cyclone, 3.72 lakh people were shifted to 10,000 shelters.
“As many as 4,470 pregnant women were shifted to safer places.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan: heavy rain lashes Srikakulam
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan: heavy rain lashes Srikakulam
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan crossed the coast close to Gopalpur in Odisha between 7.30 a.m. and 8.30 a.m. on Friday and weakened into a deep depression.
Srikakulam district was spared the extensive damage seen during earlier cyclones, though heavy rain lashed parts of it.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the cyclonic storm made landfall with winds of 70 to 80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph.
By 2.30 p.m., the system lay about 100 km west-northwest of Puri, moving northwards.
It was expected to weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over the following nine hours.

In the 23 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Friday, Ichchapuram recorded 168.75 mm of rain, followed by Arakabadra (162.5 mm), Kanchili (148.5 mm), MS Pally (146.25 mm) and Korlam (128.75 mm), according to the IMD.
District officials said Srikakulam district recorded a cumulative rainfall of 908.4 mm across its mandals, an average of 30.3 mm, in the 24 hours ending 8 a.m.
Light rain continued during the day.

Data from the Directorate of Economics and Statistics showed the following readings between 8.30 a.m. and 6 p.m.: Kothakota and Cherlopalem in Anakapalli district recorded 16.5 mm each, D. Polavaram in Kakinada district 12 mm, Makkuva in Parvathipuram Manyam district 5 mm, Masada in Alluri Sitharama Raju district 1.5 mm, Lingapalem in Eluru district 1.25 mm and Padmanabhapuram in Visakhapatnam district 0.75 mm.
Day temperatures stayed below normal along the north coast, according to the IMD’s Meteorological Centre, Amaravati.
Visakhapatnam recorded a maximum of 29°C, 1.2°C below normal, and Tuni 27.8°C, 4°C below normal.
Amaravati recorded 32.4°C. Kavali was the warmest among the stations reported, at 35.2°C, 4.5°C above normal.

stories.summary: Poonch, Nov 20: General Officer Commanding (GOC) Northern Command Lieutenant General Pratik Sharma on Friday visited forward posts in the Poonch and Sunderbani sectors along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir to review the prevailing security situation and assess operational preparedness of troops. Dung the visit, the Army Commander was briefed on the operational environment, counter infiltration measures, joint intelligence framework and synergy with other key stakeholders. Interacting with troops, the Army Commander commended them for their high morale, professionalism and resolute commitment towards safeguarding the nation.

stories.headline: The Summit Meetings
stories.title: The Summit Meetings
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Manila this week to participate in three important summit meetings. Of these the QUAD Summit has attracted the most attention in the Indian media. Of the other two the India-Asean Summit has got more attention than the East Asia Summit (EAS). However, for India’s interests all three were significant though in different ways. There were also two common denominators in all three and this writer turns to them at the outset. The first common element, though unmentioned, is the rise of China which is now so advanced that it forms a virtual G2 with the world’s leading power, the United States. The Asean countries live in the shadow of China. Of these Myanmar, Thailand, Laos and Vietnam share land boundaries while the seven other Asean states are greatly impacted by it. The Chinese have always sought to exercise influence in the Asean countries but earlier, before, they became the world’s second largest economy and a scientific and technological power, the US was predominant in most of the Asean states. That is not clear cut now. All Asean countries are trying to navigate their diplomatic path carefully and avoid alienating either of the two powers. They wish to hedge their bets not only between the two but also want other powers, especially India, to enhance its involvement in Asean so that they can balance their foreign policies between major powers. The second element is the Asean desire that its centrality in the region should be acknowledged. The EAS, which includes eight of Asean’s twelve dialogue partners, mentioned this directly in its Joint Declaration. The eight are India, Australia, New Zealand, China, Japan, South Korea, US and Russia. The Declaration declared the EAS member states commitment to “Maintain and support Asean’s unity and centrality in ASEAN-led mechanisms, reaffirming Asean’s role as the anchor of the EAS framework and in shaping an evolving regional architecture that is open, resilient, transparent, and upholds international law, and support Asean in playing a bigger role in international affairs”. The fact is that a reference to Asean centrality is good to give the group the feeling that it is not allowing any single power to dominate the region or its affairs. It is also helpful to the non-Asean EAS major states that are its members to exercise a degree of self-restraint in extending their influence in the grouping lest their competition brings about great turmoil in a part of the world which has witnessed substantial growth over the past many decades. This self-restraint does not mean that the US and China and even India are not doing their best to enhance their ties comprehensively with Asean states. India had cordial ties with Asean member countries before the organisation came into existence in 1967. On its part, the group wished to draw India in but it was unwilling to do so. Indian priorities were different during the Cold War and it was indifferent to their desire to intensify relations. Besides then the Asean countries model of development and that of India was vastly apart. The liberalisation of the Indian economy and the end of the Cold War changed Indian priorities. Prime Minister Narasimha Rao coined the term ‘Look East’ to signal India’s transformed outlook towards Asean but the Asean countries, particularly Malaysia under Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, dragged its feet. It was left to Singapore to insist within Asean forums that India was going to emerge as one of the largest economies of the world and that its weight in world affairs was growing though in a benign way. Hence, India’s status should be raised from an initial sectoral dialogue partner to that of a full partner and also be included in EAS when it was established in 2005. Earlier Asean and India agreed to begin an annual summit process in 2002 with the first summit held in Phnom Penh in November that year. This year’s summit in which Modi, who modified Look East to Act East, led the Indian delegation was the 23rd one. It was also Modi’s 13th. Summing up the direction of this summit Rudrendra Tandon, Secretary East in the Ministry of External Affairs mentioned that Modi told the Asean leaders “... given the geopolitical situation that both India as well as ASEAN member states face, and given India and ASEAN member states’ commonalities, our common values, our common ways of looking at international developments, and our very close people-to-people ties which are rooted in antiquity, India and ASEAN member states must work together to become drivers of stability in Asia”. For this purpose he made some specific suggestions. Tandon noted that these were that Indian and Asean must cooperate in the maritime domain, both should collaborate to combat transnational crime, particularly cyber crime and fraud, cooperate in developing resilient supply chains in the area of critical minerals, that “both India and Asean member states need to move away from being mere consumers of technology to becoming co-creators of technology” and that both needed to upgrade people-to-people contacts and tourism. It may be mentioned that Indians are already travelling in great numbers to some Asean destinations and now India must do more to attract Asean tourists beyond the Buddhist circuit. In his address to EAS Modi emphasised as Tandon put it “ peace, stability, and predictability in interstate relations”. He also called for “dialogue, mutual respect, and collaboration…”. Modi has stressed this approach since the beginning of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. However, till now Russia and the US who as members of the P5 are responsible for the maintenance of international peace and security have paid scant regard to following the path of peace.

stories.title: Technology created vistas for cultural connectivity, says PM Modi
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday emphasised the significance of holding a dialogue on civilisational connections in India at a time when global discussions are "dominated by war and unrest", asserting that cultural connections serve as the "strongest guarantee" for world peace. In his address after inaugurating the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum being hosted at the historic Purana Quila in Delhi, he also noted that cultural and civilisational cooperation among member countries of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) can further strengthen these ties. "Empires have certainly changed the maps of the world, but civilisational dialogues have changed the ideas of the world and enriched them," he said at the forum, attended by delegates from various SCO member countries, including Pakistan minister Musadik Malik. A mega cultural programme themed on 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakum' (world is one family) was showcased to the delegates, depicting the civilisational linkages of .

stories.headline: Chief Justice visits District Court Complex Budgam
stories.title: Chief Justice visits District Court Complex Budgam
stories.summary: Budgam, Nov 20: Dr. Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati, Chief Justice, High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, accompanied by Justice Sindhu Sharma, Administrative Judge for District Budgam, today visited District Court Complex, Budgam. The Chief Justice was accorded a ceremonial Guard of Honour and was warmly welcomed by the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Budgam, O.P. Bhagat. Deputy Commissioner Budgam Jatin Kishore, Senior Superintendent of Police Budgam Hariprasad KK, along with other judicial and administrative officers, were present on the occasion. Judges from the Registry, M.K. Sharma, Registrar General, Haq Nawaz Zargar, Principal Secretary to the Chief Justice, members of the District Judiciary, court staff, officials of the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) and Para Legal Volunteers (PLVs) were also present. The Chief Justice, in his address, emphasised the collective responsibility of the Bar, Bench and administration in strengthening the justice delivery system and upholding public trust. He highlighted the importance of adopting emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence, with due caution to enhance transparency, efficiency and speedy delivery of justice. Dr. Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati stressed the need to strengthen the Bar and Bench, promote better facilities and opportunities for women lawyers, and uphold the highest standards of professionalism and judicial accountability. Referring to the forthcoming centenary celebrations of the judicial institution on 28th March 2027, he called upon all members of the legal fraternity across Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh to actively participate in this historic milestone and reaffirm their commitment to justice and public service. He assured that suggestions for institutional improvement would be considered. The presence of Justice Sindhu Sharma was particularly significant in view of her administrative association with the district. The occasion provided an opportunity to acknowledge the role of the District Judiciary in ensuring effective judicial administration and the importance of coordinated efforts among all institutions associated with the justice delivery mechanism. The District Bar Association Budgam, through its President, submitted a memorandum seeking urgent intervention for strengthening judicial infrastructure in the district. The key demands included construction of a new Court Complex at Budgam, establishment of a separate NIA Court and additional judicial courts, construction of Court Complexes at Charar-i-Sharief and Beerwah and a Munsiff Court at Khansahib, provision of additional advocates’ chambers, upgradation of the Ladies’ Bar Room, development of parking facilities, and construction of separate photocopy and canteen facilities for advocates. The Association emphasised that these measures are essential for improving judicial efficiency, addressing infrastructural deficiencies, facilitating the legal fraternity and ensuring better access and convenience for litigants and the general public. The programme was also attended by advocates from all four Tehsils of District Budgam, represented by their respective Bar Association Presidents. A significant highlight of the occasion was the release of the magazine published by the District Legal Services Authority, Budgam, under the supervision and guidance of J&K Legal Services Authority, by the Chief Justice, Dr. Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati (Patron-in-Chief, J&K Legal Services Authority). The programme concluded with a formal Vote of Thanks presented by Additional District Judge Budgam, Yahya Firdous.

stories.title: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on deepathoon at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement
stories.summary: A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice

corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) allowed the lighting of the lamp, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, on the ‘Deepathoon’ at the Thirupparankundram Hill on Karthigai Deepam day (November 24, 2026).

A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the ‘Deepathoon’ as an essential practice.
The court issued notice on the appeals filed by the State.

The interim order dealt with pleas by the State to stay the January 6 judgment and also looked into the question whether the lamp could be lit on the ‘Deepathoon’ on the forthcoming Karthigai Deepam festival day falling on November 24.

Pronouncing the interim order, Justice Kumar said the court was aware of the dangers of allowing once becoming a precedent, while also noting that two separate Benches of the High Court had allowed the lighting of the lamp.
Imposing restrictions and safeguards, the Supreme Court directed that the Devasthanam would exclusively decide the members of the team to light the lamp on November 24.
The Madurai District Collector would act as nodal officer for the event.
The Commissioner of Madurai.
Police has to provide the ring of security.
The Centre was directed to supplement security arrangements with CRPF personnel, if required.
No procession, slogan-raising or permission to gathering of general public will be allowed, the court directed.
The access to lamp-lighting would be allowed to only authorised persons.

stories.headline: BJP, Congress open accounts in LAHDC polls
stories.title: BJP, Congress open accounts in LAHDC polls
stories.summary: Kargil, Nov 20: Ahead of the December 4 polling for the eight Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDCs), both the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Indian National Congress (INC) have officially opened their accounts, with one candidate from each party elected unopposed following the expiry of the nomination withdrawal deadline on Friday, November 20, 2026. The early breakthroughs come as electioneering intensifies across the Union Territory for the expanded 100-seat Hill Council framework spanning eight districts—Leh, Kargil, Nubra, Changthang, Zanskar, Sham, Sankoo, and Drass. For the BJP, candidate Dorjey Angchuk was declared elected unopposed from the Samad-Kharnak constituency of the Changthang Hill Council after no rival nominations remained in the fray. As the deadline for the withdrawal of nominations passed today, Angchuk was the sole contender in the remote, high-altitude constituency. The early breakthrough has energised the party's camp ahead of the December 4 polling across all eight districts of the Union Territory. Hailing the development as a morale booster for the party's grassroots campaign, former Ladakh MP and BJP candidate from Leh’s Solar Colony constituency, Jamyang Tsering Namgyal, called it “a wonderful beginning to the party’s march towards victory.” “A wonderful beginning to our march towards victory,” celebrated former BJP Lok Sabha MP Jamyang Tsering Namgyal on social media. In a notable political move to bolster the party's grassroots campaign, Namgyal himself has returned to regional electoral politics, filing his nomination from the Solar Colony constituency in the Leh Hill Council. Simultaneously, the Congress matched the BJP's early tally, securing its first seat unopposed as the withdrawal window closed on November 20, setting the stage for a fiercely contested battle across the remaining constituencies. The Indian National Congress (INC) has officially opened its account in the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC) Kargil elections, with party candidate Sayeda Banoo elected unopposed from the Lochum constituency. The development occurred on the final day for nomination withdrawal, following a major political consensus in the constituency. Independent candidate Kaneez Fatima, along with another contesting candidate, formally withdrew their nomination papers in favour of Sayeda Banoo. With no other contenders remaining in the fray after the deadline expired, the Returning Officer declared Banoo elected unopposed. Political observers note that the early uncontested victory provides a significant morale boost to the Congress party unit in Kargil as campaigning intensifies across the remaining council seats. Party leaders and local supporters in Lochum welcomed the outcome, hailing the withdrawal of the independent candidate as a gesture of unity and confidence in Banoo's leadership and development agenda for the region. According to election officials, a total of 541 nominations were filed across the 100 constituencies, with independent contenders making up the largest share of candidates. Among the major political parties, the Congress and the BJP have fielded candidates across almost all constituencies, while the Jammu and Kashmir National Conference (JKNC) is contesting a smaller number of seats following recent organisational shifts in the region. Notably, three constituencies did not receive any nominations. This year's LAHDC polls mark a historic milestone in Ladakh's local governance. Following the creation of six new districts alongside Leh and Kargil, the total number of council seats was expanded to 100, with 36 seats reserved for women for the first time. Meanwhile, polling for the remaining contested seats is scheduled to take place on December 4, even as regional outfits—including the Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA)—continue to press their demands for constitutional safeguards and the deferment of winter elections. The entire electoral process is slated to conclude by December 8.
